subject: Order form invoice path & tax: clearinghouse proposal for SynTech
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <finance@syntech.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@syntech.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SynTech order form — invoice entity & tax handling questions

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has a few open items on the Order Form we need to close before we can issue a PO:

- Which Redwood legal entity will issue invoices for the SynTech contract? We need to align the invoice recipient and VAT treatment.
- Net terms: SynTech requests Net 45. Would Redwood accept Net 45 (or Net 60) for the first 12 months?
- Minimum commits phasing: can we receive staged invoicing when commits are phased?
- If SynTech provides a VAT registration (EU), can invoices be issued from your EU entity to make VAT 0% reverse charge? Or do we need to accept US invoices and self-report?

I attached our procurement template (SynTech_PO_req.pdf) and highlighted a few fields. Can you share a proposed invoice flow and any redline language your legal team will require?

Target: sign by 10/29 if possible — procurement is on a tight cycle.

Thanks,
Samantha Cole
Finance Manager, SynTech
finance@syntech.com
Attachment: SynTech_PO_req.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <finance@syntech.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SynTech order form — invoice entity & tax handling questions

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Putting three pragmatic options on the table so procurement can pick the one that fits SynTech's accounting:

1) Default US invoicing (fastest): Redwood (US) issues invoices to SynTech US entity. Customer self-reports VAT where applicable. Net 45 available.

2) EU entity path (requires VAT cert + PO to EU entity): Redwood will issue from Redwood EU entity; reverse-charge possible if you provide VAT registration and an EU PO. This adds ~3 business days for finance alignment.

3) Clearinghouse split (recommended for phased commits): Redwood issues a primary invoice from Redwood US and secondary pro-forma / attachment noting EU-taxable lines; final invoice split triggered by PO and VAT evidence. This minimizes procurement friction for phased minimum commits.

I attached a short diagram (proposed-invoice-flow-v1.pdf). From an ops perspective, option 3 reduces rework when commits are staggered and when you need invoice splits per quarter.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly / legal to confirm required Order Form redlines for invoice-split and tax indemnity.
- If SynTech confirms VAT certificate delivery, we'll populate EU entity fields and provide DocuSign-ready Order Form.
- Karthik to confirm billing cadence for phased minimum commits (how you want line-item phasing reflected).

If that plan looks good, I'll draft the mutual action items and circulate an updated Order Form by EOD.

— Logan
Director, Commercials 
Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-invoice-flow-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Samantha Cole <finance@syntech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SynTech order form — invoice entity & tax handling questions

Thanks Logan — looping in legal/ops comments. Samantha, quick summary of proposed redlines we'll include in the Order Form / Appendix:

1) Invoice recipient: default Redwood, Inc. (US) unless Customer provides valid local tax registration and PO referencing Redwood [EU Entity]. If Customer provides VAT registration prior to commencement, Redwood will invoice from Redwood Ltd. (EU) and apply reverse charge where permitted.

2) Net terms: Redwood can accept Net 45. We'll keep standard late payment interest clause (1.5%/month) and a right to suspend service for overdue balances after 30 days' written notice.

3) Minimum commit / phased invoicing: add an "Invoice Split" appendix that enables staged invoicing per mutually agreed schedule. Appendix will define tranche percentages, invoicing triggers, and pro rata reconciliation at quarter close.

4) Tax indemnity: Customer is responsible for local taxes, duties, and withholding. Where Redwood invoices from a non-local entity, Customer shall provide evidence of tax residency to avoid withholding.

5) Evidence & timing: Customer to provide VAT certificate and PO within 10 business days of signature to enable entity swap. If evidence is not provided, Redwood will issue from Redwood (US) and Customer accepts responsibility for any local VAT withholdings.

I'm attaching tracked redlines for the Order Form (orderform-redlines-track-changes.docx). Karthik: please confirm whether the "Invoice Split" appendix needs a sample phasing table or if we can keep it prose and finalize the table in SOW / PO.

Samantha — if SynTech agrees to the above, I'll incorporate the clauses and produce a DocuSign-ready Order Form.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts 
Redwood Inference
Attachment: orderform-redlines-track-changes.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Michael Lee <michael.lee@syntech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Samantha Cole <finance@syntech.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SynTech order form — invoice entity & tax handling questions

Kimberly / Logan — thanks for the clear options and redlines. SynTech can:

- Accept Net 45.
- Provide VAT registration (if needed) within 7 business days after the signed order form.
- We prefer the clearinghouse split (option 3) for the staged commits — that matches our internal ERP mapping.

Please do the following so procurement can finalize:
1) Circulate a two-line Mutual Action Plan with milestone dates (signature, VAT certificate, invoice split triggers).
2) Produce the DocuSign-ready Order Form with the Invoice Split appendix populated with a placeholder phasing table (we will update the exact % once finance confirms).

Once we have that, SynTech procurement will issue the PO and sign. I attached our PO for reference (SynTech_PO_2026_9874.pdf).

Appreciate the quick turn.

— Michael Lee
Senior Procurement Lead, SynTech
Attachment: SynTech_PO_2026_9874.pdf (application/pdf)
